imp.generic: He left the house feeling sad and went for a walk.
imp.author: He came down the steps of the house in Eccles Street and stood a moment in the grey light, settling his hat, and there was nothing now to keep him in the city and nothing to take him out of it.

imp.generic: She was late, and he started to worry she wouldn't come.
imp.author: When the half hour struck and she had not come he told himself she had been kept by her mother, that the trams were slow, and he waited until the lamps were lit and the platform emptied.

imp.generic: He had always planned to write his brother but never did.
imp.author: He had meant, for years now, to write to his brother in Cork, and each Sunday he told himself the letter would be written.

imp.generic: The old man remembered a girl he had once loved.
imp.author: He was thinking of a winter long ago when he had walked a girl home along the canal at Portobello, and he could not now recall her face, only the cold of it and the way the gaslight had lain in pools along the path.

imp.generic: He felt guilty about the money he had stolen.
imp.author: He thought of the half-crown he had taken from her purse and spent on toffee and the music-hall, and how he had told himself it was nothing, and now the nothing sat in his chest like a swallowed stone.

imp.generic: It was a cold evening and the streetlights were coming on.
imp.author: The fields beyond were a soft grey nothing and somewhere a dog barked twice and was quiet, and he felt the chill of the stone come through his coat.

imp.generic: The party guests talked about local gossip and avoided serious topics.
imp.author: The talk went round, as it always went, to the funerals of the season and the price of coal and the disgrace of young Lacey who had gone to America and never written; nobody spoke of the war.

imp.generic: He resolved to be a better person, as he did every year.
imp.author: He had meant to be good; he had meant it every year and every year the meaning wore thin by Easter, like the elbows of his jacket.

imp.generic: He didn't want to admit what he was really feeling.
imp.author: Still he stood, the brooch growing cold against him, unwilling yet to give it the name it had.

imp.generic: He went back inside to eat dinner alone.
imp.author: He turned and went back up the steps and let himself in, and the hall was dark and smelled faintly of damp and of the dinner he would eat alone.
